findings.title: Care grounds gratitude within its limit
findings.claim: The sequence from maternal pregnancy through compounded weakness to two-year weaning gives the command to thank God and parents a material ground; the next ayah keeps gratitude distinct from coerced obedience.
findings.mechanism: The focus words for mother, pregnancy, weakness, weaning, the yearly cycle, and gratitude carry one embodied care sequence. The host basmala's mercy language and 31:12's command to gratitude prepare its frame. Then 31:15 refuses obedience under parental pressure while preserving good companionship, so the bodily weaning boundary resonates with a later relational boundary without ceasing to mean weaning.
findings.reader_payoff: Gratitude to parents becomes recognition of costly, embodied care, while the following instruction makes its limit clear: care invites thanks and companionship, not surrender of religious judgment.
findings.containment: Pregnancy, repeated weakness, and the two-year weaning period remain literal features of the focus. Their relation to 31:15 is a pericope-level echo, not a claim that the two years cause adulthood or that gratitude requires unrestricted obedience; 31:15 may also be read as addressing its specific theological conflict.

epistemic.reason: The candidate supports and accepted focus branch records ground the care sequence, and the supplied 31:12 and 31:15 surfaces ground its context. Reading bodily weaning as an echo of the later moral boundary remains interpretive rather than lexical.

findings.title: Weaning and a boundary within filiality
findings.claim: The focus's literal weaning term also carries a contextual echo of moral differentiation: 31:15 refuses parental pressure to associate partners with God while preserving good companionship with the parents.
findings.mechanism: The focus word فِصَال carries an accepted boundary facet alongside its ordinary weaning sense. The immediately following ayah supplies separate acts of pressure, refused obedience, continued companionship, recognized good, and following another path. Their contact with the focus's parent-child separation image makes the relation legible as a boundary that can preserve the bond while refusing a demand.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can hold together gratitude and companionship with parents and a clear limit on the acts one may follow them into.
findings.containment: The focus continues to say weaning; the moral boundary is an attributed contextual resonance, not a lexical replacement or a claim that bodily weaning causes later independence. A live alternative keeps 31:15 within its stated theological exception rather than treating it as a general theory of adulthood.

epistemic.reason: The focus boundary branch is independently registered and the HFT context coordinates, roots, and roles agree with the supplied 31:15 Arabic. The HFT's extension from bodily to moral separation remains attributed, with its narrower alternative preserved.

findings.title: Hidden and manifest phases of care
findings.claim: The later pairing of outward and inward blessings casts maternal pregnancy and the child's weaning as hidden and manifest phases of care, while the focus's gratitude responds to both.
findings.mechanism: حَمَلَتْهُ carries the registered pregnancy facet and ٱشْكُرْ carries the registered recognition-of-favor facet. In 31:20, the supplied HFT trace connects the inward and visible terms and the words for provision and favor to these focus occurrences. The contact makes pregnancy and later care legible as phases within one blessing rather than unrelated facts supporting an obligation.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see the focus's bodily sequence as a movement from concealed formation toward manifest care, and gratitude as the response to both phases.
findings.containment: 31:20 speaks generally of God's favors and does not explicitly single out maternal care. The specific mapping to pregnancy and weaning is retained as HFT-attributed contextual inference; the general outward/inward reading remains intact.
